name: Event Generating Consumer
helpText:
Event Generating Consumer

Consumers provide the 'glue' between the entry into the flow and the underlying technology generating the event. In order to create your own consumer you need to implement Consumer Interface.
allowableProperties_comment: Note that the order of properties in this file dictates the order displayed on screen, unless propertyDisplayOrder is set, which will be used as the primary key

componentName.helpText: The name of the component as displayed on diagrams. The name should be unique for the flow. The name will be used internally to reflect the bean created.

endpointEventProvider.helpText: Provide the class that supplies the events this consumer generates: implement getEvent() to return each event in turn and rollback() to handle retry of the current event. EventGeneratingConsumer is typically used to provision test or demonstration flows quickly, so this is usually a small bespoke class you write yourself - there is no meaningful pre-built implementation to reuse.
endpointEventProvider.validationMessage: Provide a java classname for the endpoint event provider bean.

managedEventIdentifierService.helpText: Optional, and safe to leave unset for most flows. Ikasan gives every message a tracking ID as it processes it - used to correlate a message in the audit trail/dashboard, and to recognise the same message again if a flow error 'parks' it for later retry. By default this ID is just a raw hash of the message content (functional, but not human-readable). Setting this property lets you supply your own class to derive a more meaningful ID instead, e.g. from a business key in the message payload.
managedEventIdentifierService.validationMessage: Provide a java classname for the endpoint event provider bean.
